confirmed.title: Every shared control primitive is defined twice (globals.css + kernel.css) in two conflicting token vocabularies — the root cause of the component forks
confirmed.evidence: `.btn` is defined at both globals.css:1947 and kernel.css:712; `.badge` at globals.css:1912 and kernel.css:949; `.pill` at globals.css:1832 and kernel.css:981; `input.inp` at globals.css:2247 and kernel.css:790. The two disagree on tokens — e.g. globals `.badge { border-radius: 999px; border-color: rgba(76,183,130,0.35) }` vs kernel `.badge { border-radius: var(--radius); border-color: color-mix(in srgb, var(--flood) 60%, transparent) }`.
confirmed.user_impact: kernel.css wins only where a selector exists in both files (load order); wherever kernel never redefined a selector — `.chip`, `.link`, `.toggle`, and almost every card/list class — the component keeps the OLD globals treatment (teal `--accent`, pill-shaped badges, rgba literals, mono chips). This split is why sibling elements in one row belong to two visual systems, and why 'fix the button' or 'fix the chip' has to be done twice or is silently reverted by the losing definition.
confirmed.fix: Treat kernel.css as the single source for the shared primitives: move the surviving old-system selectors (`.chip`, `.link`, `.toggle`, the card/list families) into the kernel vocabulary, then delete the duplicated `.btn`/`.badge`/`.pill`/`.inp` blocks from globals.css so each primitive is defined exactly once. This also directly serves the 800-line ceiling by letting globals.css shrink to only truly page-specific rules.

confirmed.title: Card/panel treatments have forked across at least six variants that disagree on radius, padding and border weight

Radius (0/4/8/12), padding (12px / 18px / 22-24px / 30px) and border (hairline / 1px / 0.5px rgba literal) all disagree, so no two card surfaces feel like the same material. `connector-card` radius 0, `resource-card` 12px and `recipe-card`'s 12px fallback are all off the approved {4px, 8px} scale.

Correct connector-card to `var(--radius)`, and map resource-card/recipe-card 12px onto 8px. Delete the 0.5px rgba literal border in favor of the hairline token.

confirmed.title: `.chip` was never migrated to the kernel idiom, so it renders in the old design system next to kernel-styled `.badge`/`.pill`
confirmed.evidence: kernel.css redefines .badge and .pill (lines 944-1013) but contains ZERO `.chip` rules (`grep -n '\.chip' kernel.css` returns nothing); the only `.chip` definition remains in globals.css:2845 — `font-family: var(--font-mono); font-size: 11px; ... border: 1px solid var(--border); border-radius: 6px;`

confirmed.title: The org-entry form has no error surface; an unknown or misspelled org navigates full-page to an API endpoint and renders the raw control-plane response.
confirmed.user_impact: Submit does a top-level browser navigation to the proxy start endpoint; the only client validation is non-empty (`disabled={busy || org.trim() === ""}`). On the happy path the control plane answers a 302 to the IdP. But any non-redirect rejection (unknown org, disabled org, 4xx/5xx) is returned by the proxy as its body with the upstream content-type, so the browser paints raw JSON/text as a full page. The button is stuck on 'Redirecting…', the user has left the styled shell entirely, there is no inline 'organization not found' message, and no way back — the worst possible first-run failure. The form comment even says it 'never enumerates organizations', but nothing tells the user their org was wrong.
confirmed.fix: Resolve the org via a fetch first (or intercept the error response) and render an inline field error inside the panel; keep the user on the styled /login surface instead of navigating them into a raw API response.

confirmed.title: The run timeline and status pill update over SSE/polling but are not a live region, so a screen reader hears nothing

confirmed.title: SectionReveal can leave server-rendered content stranded at opacity:0 (blank viewport / half-faded section)
confirmed.evidence: for (const s of sections) s.classList.add("st-reveal"); ... if (e.isIntersecting) { e.target.classList.add("in"); io.unobserve(e.target); }  (paired with .st-reveal { opacity: 0; transform: translateY(16px); } in globals.css:6236)
confirmed.user_impact: Two real failure modes. (1) On every load the effect adds st-reveal (opacity:0) to sections the server already rendered visible, but the IntersectionObserver first callback is asynchronous, so any above-the-fold non-hero section paints, goes blank, then fades back in (flash of hidden content). (2) The callback ONLY adds `in` when isIntersecting is true and has no fallback; on a fast programmatic scroll or a #hash landing, a section that crosses from below-viewport to above-viewport between IO deliveries is reported not-intersecting, never gets `in`, and stays permanently at opacity 0 unless the user scrolls back over it. This is the mechanism behind the observed blank viewport and half-faded section.
confirmed.fix: Do not hide content the observer might never re-reveal. Either (a) gate the initial hide so only sections currently below the fold get st-reveal (measure getBoundingClientRect().top > innerHeight before adding the class), or (b) add a safety net: after IO disconnect / a short timeout, force `in` on any still-unrevealed section, and reveal on the observer first batch rather than waiting for an intersecting entry. Keep the reduced-motion early-return.
confirmed.correction: The 'permanently at opacity 0' wording overstates it: sections that were never unobserved recover the moment they scroll back into view, so the stranding self-heals on scroll. The reliably visible defect is the blank-content window on reload/scroll-restore plus the above-the-fold hide-then-fade flash. Mechanism and file/line are exact.

confirmed.title: The run-detail timeline renders no timestamp on any event, so the product's core audit surface cannot say when anything happened.
confirmed.user_impact: A human watching an agent hit the policy gate, or auditing a finished run, sees an ordered list of verdicts and tool calls with no time on any row. They cannot tell whether a deny happened one second or ten minutes after the request, how long the agent stalled before an approval, or when the run actually ended — the exact facts a governance/audit timeline exists to provide.
confirmed.fix: EventRow already carries `occurred_at` (app/lib/api.ts:803) and bits.tsx already exports `timeAgo()`; render a mono time in the tl-line (a relative `timeAgo(ev.occurred_at)` with the absolute time in a `title=`), consistent with the identity's rule that machine-generated data uses IBM Plex Mono.

confirmed.title: A dropped live stream is completely invisible once any event has arrived — the timeline silently stops updating with no indication.
confirmed.user_impact: The `streamReconnecting` state is only surfaced inside the `events.length === 0` empty branch. On any real run — where events have already streamed in — an SSE disconnection shows nothing: the timeline just stops. A person watching a live run believes the agent is idle or finished when in fact the feed has silently broken, on the one screen where knowing the live state is the entire point.
confirmed.fix: Show the reconnecting indicator regardless of `events.length` — e.g. a small mono 'reconnecting…' chip in the `timeline` sectitle whenever `streamReconnecting`, so a dropped feed is always visible above the last-known events.

confirmed.title: AutomationActivity swallows its load error and renders a failed fetch as "No runs yet."

On the FIRST poll failing (control plane down, 401, 500), sessions/deliveries/invocations stay [] and all three columns confidently print "No runs yet.", "No invocations yet.", "No deliveries yet." — telling the user an automation has never run when in fact the data could not be loaded. It renders both in the Overview automations tab and the automation detail page's Activity section.
confirmed.fix: Adopt the same pattern the parent AutomationPanel already uses: track a hasSnapshot boolean set true only on a fulfilled poll, and a loadErr; while !hasSnapshot show the skeleton, on error show the shared <StateError> ('activity unavailable'), and only render the 'No … yet.' empty copy once a fetch has actually succeeded.

confirmed.user_impact: The same .sectitle component renders lowercase on the run-detail page ('timeline', 'cost & usage', 'run spec', 'frozen capabilities', 'result deliveries') but Capitalized on other pages ('GitHub Apps', 'Connections' in integrations; 'Health', 'Security model' in settings; 'What it does', 'Permissions', 'Versions' in recipes). confirmed.title: Component rules hardcode hex colors that must come from tokens.
confirmed.user_impact: These charcoal/paper literals are frozen to the light theme — .btn.human and .btn.danger:hover text and the masthead approval-count badge won't invert with the charcoal dark theme, so the ink color can collide with its own fill in dark mode. They also duplicate values the token layer already owns (#1c2024 = --ds-gray-1000/--flood-ink, #faf9f2 = --ds-background-200).
confirmed.fix: Replace the literals with the existing tokens: #1c2024 → var(--flood-ink) (or var(--ds-gray-1000)) and #faf9f2 → var(--ds-background-200). No hex outside the :root/[data-theme] blocks.
confirmed.correction: The core defect (literal hex in component rules) is solid and is the reportable violation. The secondary claim that these 'won't invert in dark mode and collide with their own fill' is speculative — .btn.human/.btn.danger fills are var(--gold)/var(--ds-red-700) and were not confirmed to invert into a clash; report the token-rule violation, not the collision.

confirmed.title: Three parallel token vocabularies encode one palette; #f2f0e7 is hard-coded in at least four places
confirmed.evidence: --bg: #f2f0e7;   (globals :root)  |  --st-bg: #f2f0e7; (globals:5819)  |  --bg: #f2f0e7; (globals:5907, .st scope)  |  --ds-background-100: #f2f0e7; (kernel:16)
confirmed.user_impact: The same canvas color is declared under three unrelated naming systems (--*, --st-* for marketing, --ds-* for the kernel layer) plus a scoped re-declaration on .st. Changing the paper color correctly requires editing four literals across two files and three namespaces; miss one and the marketing site, docs, and dashboard drift apart. This is why 'all colour must come from a token' is not enough — the tokens themselves are triplicated.
confirmed.fix: Collapse to one token set in a single tokens.css. Define the palette once as the canonical --* tokens; make --st-* and --ds-* aliases that reference the canonical token (e.g. --ds-background-100: var(--bg)) rather than re-stating the hex.
confirmed.correction: Understated if anything: #f2f0e7 appears MORE than four times (also --primary-ink at globals:47 and kernel:74, and fill at globals:7431). The 'at least four' hedge is safe and the finding holds.

confirmed.title: Tailwind is imported but never used — dead engine plus a Preflight reset that can collide with the hand-rolled resets
confirmed.evidence: @import "tailwindcss";
confirmed.user_impact: There is no tailwind.config, zero @theme/@apply/@utility/@variant directives in either file, and effectively no utility classes among the 2074 className attributes in the .tsx — every style is hand-written custom CSS. The import still pulls Tailwind's Preflight reset and utility machinery into the bundle, adding weight and a base-layer reset that can silently fight the codebase's own element resets.
confirmed.fix: Remove the `@import "tailwindcss";` line and verify no visual regression (the app does not consume any Tailwind utility). If a reset is wanted, keep an explicit hand-rolled one instead of Preflight.

confirmed.title: Marketing component rules hardcode off-palette hex/rgb colours instead of tokens.

confirmed.title: Raw snake_case enum values are rendered directly to users

confirmed.title: Bare status enum tokens are shown verbatim with inconsistent casing

confirmed.title: Two dark-filled primary buttons are on screen at once, so neither reads as the page's primary action.

confirmed.title: Checkboxes have no shared primitive; accent styling is declared per-wrapper, so checkboxes outside those wrappers render the native browser-blue
confirmed.evidence: PolicyLimits.tsx:326 `<input type="checkbox" checked={net.require_approval} ... />` sits in a `<label className="field">`; `accent-color: var(--accent)` is declared only on `.check input` (globals.css:2287), `.cap-row input` (globals.css:2797) and `.recipe-choice input` (globals.css:7943) — `.field` has no such rule, and there is no global `input[type=checkbox]` accent rule.
confirmed.user_impact: Toggling a policy checkbox shows the operating-system default blue checkbox — a color absent from the entire warm-paper/charcoal/chartreuse palette — because accent-color is only wired inside three specific list wrappers. Any checkbox authored outside them (PolicyLimits `.field`, and future ones) silently leaks native blue. Meanwhile a fully-styled `.toggle` switch component exists in globals.css:2289 but is used nowhere, so the same boolean is a raw checkbox everywhere.
confirmed.fix: Add a single global `input[type=checkbox], input[type=radio] { accent-color: var(--flood); }` (or a Checkbox/Toggle primitive in bits.tsx), and remove the three per-wrapper accent declarations. Decide whether booleans are checkboxes or the existing `.toggle` switch and use one consistently; delete the dead one.

confirmed.title: An operationally critical warning is clipped mid-word because a nowrap/ellipsis rule on .task truncates the block-level second line.
confirmed.user_impact: The GitHub-App row nests a `display:block` second line inside `.task` (app/app/integrations/page.tsx:229-232) reading 'webhook → … · events disabled (no webhook secret — recreate the app)'. Because the parent `.task` forces `white-space:nowrap; overflow:hidden`, that line clips to 'events disabled (no webhook se…' and the remedy — 'recreate the app' — is cut off entirely. The single sentence telling an operator why events are dead and how to fix it is the part that gets truncated.

confirmed.title: `enter` entrance animation (translateY slide-up) has no prefers-reduced-motion override
confirmed.evidence: .home-hero (globals.css:660) `animation: enter 0.55s cubic-bezier(0.2, 0.7, 0.2, 1) both;` - also .attention-section (766), .recent-heading (774), .operate-view/.operate-tabs (1166). @keyframes enter { from { opacity:0; transform: translateY(8px) } } (1753). The seven prefers-reduced-motion blocks disable blink, .tl-item/fadein, shimmer, rc-reveal and lr-blink - none disables `enter`, and kernel.css only sets animation:none on .ops-strip/.configuration-section/.run-list/.creation-stage, not on these.

confirmed.title: "Resources" and "Activity" highlight as if you are inside a section, but clicking them navigates away to an anchor on a different page.
confirmed.evidence: const resourcesActive = ["/app/agents", "/app/capabilities", "/app/integrations"].some(...);  // then:  <Link className={resourcesActive ? "active" : ""} href="/app#configuration" ...>Resources</Link>
confirmed.user_impact: On /app/agents the "Resources" item is lit as the current location, but activating it throws the user back to an anchor section of the Overview page — the highlight promises "you are here" while the link means "go somewhere else", so the nav model is unlearnable.
confirmed.fix: Pick one model. Either make Resources and Activity real routes (/app/resources, /app/activity) that the sub-pages live under so active-styling and navigation agree, or — keeping the single-Overview model — demote them to non-highlighting section jump-links visually distinct from the true routes (Recipes/Governance/Settings) which correctly use pathname.startsWith. Do not apply .active (a location signal) to a cross-page anchor.
confirmed.correction: Cited line 105 is off: the const is line 77, the className applied at 106. Severity overstated as high; this is a deliberate section-grouping pattern (a group label lit for its sub-routes that jumps to the Overview configuration hub), medium at most.

confirmed.title: The horizontal GateStrip has no column min-width, so its notes collapse to ~one word per line and 'read-only' breaks at its hyphen.
confirmed.evidence: grid-template-columns: repeat(6, minmax(0, 1fr));
confirmed.user_impact: On the /product page the six-stage gate stays a six-column grid until the 960px breakpoint (`.gate { grid-template-columns: repeat(3, minmax(0, 1fr)); }` lives inside `@media (max-width: 960px)` at line 7797). Because each track is `minmax(0, 1fr)` with no floor, in the 961px-to-~1120px window each of the six columns is only ~115px of text area (container 1200px, 40px padding, 16px+16px cell padding), and the 12px `.gate-note` strings wrap to one or two words per line. 'fork PRs stay read-only, always' breaks at the literal hyphen in 'read-only' into 'read-' / 'only,' — the exact ugly slice described. The strip is unreadable as a sequence precisely at common laptop widths.
confirmed.fix: Reflow the 6->3 columns earlier by moving the switch to the approved 1280px breakpoint (so 961-1280px shows three comfortable columns, not six starved ones), and keep the 3->1 switch at 640px. Optionally add `overflow-wrap: normal; hyphens: manual` and a small `min-width` on `.gate-note` to prevent hyphen breaks. This also removes the non-approved 960px breakpoint.
confirmed.correction: Severity overstated as high and the window is narrower than claimed: the severe band is ~961-1000px (a ~40px slice; above 1000px the 40px padding cap lets the container grow and columns ease to ~141px by 1120px), so 'common laptop widths' up to 1120px is generous. The specific assertion that 'read-only' breaks at its literal hyphen into 'read-'/'only,' is plausible (hyphen is a break opportunity) but cannot be verified by static analysis — it is embellishment, not measured fact. Degradation, not a total break.

confirmed.title: CJK title-echo fonts are loaded with only the latin subset, so the decorative Japanese/Chinese echoes have no glyph coverage in the intended Noto face.
confirmed.user_impact: The kernel.sh page-head signature stacks the page name in Japanese and Chinese (PageEcho renders literal glyphs, e.g. jp="変更履歴" sc="更新日志", styled via `.echo-jp{font-family:var(--font-jp)}` → var(--font-noto-jp)). Because next/font fetches only the 'latin' subset of these CJK families, the Noto face carries no CJK glyphs, so every echo falls through the stack to whatever system CJK font exists (or tofu/generic sans where 'Noto Sans SC' isn't installed). The deliberate multilingual signature renders in an unintended, uncontrolled typeface across all five marketing pages.
confirmed.fix: Declare the CJK subsets these families actually need (or drop the named Noto echo and accept a system CJK fallback intentionally) so the glyphs are served by the intended face.

confirmed.title: Neither new timeline events nor a newly-pending approval are announced to assistive tech; the pending-approval banner is not even a live region.

It renders as a plain `div.approval` with no `role="alert"`/`aria-live`, and the `.timeline` container (line 264) is not a live region either (only the empty state at line 260 is). confirmed.title: Section headings across dashboard pages are non-heading <div className="sectitle"> elements
confirmed.evidence: Security model
confirmed.user_impact: On Settings, Integrations, Session detail, Governance and most policy components, the visible section titles ("timeline", "cost & usage", "Security model", "Connections", "result", "changes", "Approvals", "Network", …) are plain divs, not headings. Screen-reader users cannot jump between sections by heading and the page reads as a single flat h1 with no substructure. The Recipes pages prove the intended form exists — they use `<h2 className="sectitle">` — making the div usage an inconsistency, not a constraint (grep: 39 `.sectitle` uses, most are divs).

confirmed.title: The Overview em-dash means loading, offline, AND genuine-zero — one glyph, three meanings
confirmed.evidence: const completionRate = terminal > 0 ? `${Math.round((done / terminal) * 100)}%` : "—"; … {hasSnapshot ? completionRate : "—"}
confirmed.user_impact: On a healthy but idle deployment the Success Rate tile shows "—" (terminal===0). During the first fetch every tile shows "—" (hasSnapshot false). When the control plane is down every tile shows "—" (hasSnapshot false, offline). The big number a user reads is identical in all three cases; only the tiny <small> caption disambiguates, so the headline metric cannot be trusted to mean anything.
confirmed.fix: Separate the three meanings in the primary glyph, not just the caption. Render the skeleton shimmer while !hasSnapshot && !offline, a distinct offline dash/state while offline, and reserve "—" exclusively for genuine "no terminal runs yet" (terminal===0) with a caption like "no completed runs". The <strong> must never carry loading and real-zero as the same character.
confirmed.correction: Real but overstated as high. (a) The collapse is specific to the Success Rate tile — the Active/Needs Review/Completed tiles at lines 121/131/136 show real 0 when idle (hasSnapshot true), not "—", so "every tile shows —" only holds during loading/offline, not on a healthy idle deployment. (b) Each tile's <small> caption AND the status pill (line 115: Offline/Checking/Operational) already disambiguate the three states, so it is not true that the state is untrustworthy — only that the big number alone is ambiguous. Medium is the fair severity.

confirmed.title: A missing/deleted automation shows a raw 'Error: 404' string with no framing, no Retry, no back link
confirmed.user_impact: Navigating to a deleted or mistyped automation id resolves the route, load() rejects with the api.ts message, and the page renders the literal string 'Error: 404: not found' inside a red box — no 'not found' framing, no way back to the automations list, and no Retry. It is strictly worse than every list page, which all offer a Retry affordance and a titled failure card.
confirmed.fix: Distinguish notFound from unreachable off the typed status (see api.ts finding) and render <StateNotFound> ('this automation no longer exists') with a link back to /app?view=automations for a 404, and <StateError> with a Retry for a transient failure. Never surface the raw Error string as the whole page.
confirmed.correction: Core claim confirmed. The comparative tail ('strictly worse than every list page, which all offer a Retry') was not independently verified per-page and is not load-bearing to the defect.

confirmed.title: sessions/[id] presents a 404 (nonexistent run) as a permanent 'control plane' outage
confirmed.evidence:
Run detail is unavailable.

No cost, usage, or activity assumptions were made from the failed response.
confirmed.user_impact: For a bad/expired session id the core GET rejects, hasSnapshot stays false, and the user sees 'Run detail is unavailable' with a Retry button that will never succeed — an outage story for what is actually a missing resource. The user retries indefinitely against a 404.
confirmed.fix: Branch on the failure kind: a 404 renders <StateNotFound> ('this run does not exist' + link to /app) with no Retry; a transient/5xx keeps today's 'unavailable' card with Retry. The distinction requires the typed status from api.ts below.

confirmed.title: api.ts collapses every non-2xx into one opaque Error string, making 404-vs-down impossible to tell apart downstream
confirmed.evidence: throw new Error(`${res.status}: ${await res.text()}`);
confirmed.user_impact: Because the status is stringified into the message, every consumer must string-match (the codebase already does e.message.startsWith("404") in fetchConnectionTools) to recover it. Most pages don't, so they cannot render a not-found state distinct from an outage — the root cause of the two findings above. This is the single missing primitive the whole state system needs.
confirmed.fix: Throw a typed error carrying the numeric status, e.g. class ApiError extends Error { status: number }, from fetchGet and every apiPost/Put/Patch/Delete. Then the shared <StateError>/<StateNotFound> and the detail pages can branch on err.status === 404 vs >=500/network without string parsing.

confirmed.title: notFound() is actively called from the docs routes but no not-found boundary exists to catch it

confirmed.title: No motion token scale - 16 hand-picked durations and 7 timing functions, same value spelled two ways
confirmed.evidence: Durations in use: 0.1s/100ms, 0.12s/120ms, 0.13s/130ms, 0.15s, 0.16s, 180ms, 0.2s, 0.22s, 0.3s, 0.35s, 0.4s, 0.5s, 0.55s, 1.1s, 1.4s, 1.45s. e.g. globals.css:4266 `transition: opacity 120ms ease-out;` vs globals.css:381 `transition: background 0.12s, color 0.12s;` - identical duration, two spellings. Timing functions: bare `ease` x41, `cubic-bezier(0.2, 0.7, 0.2, 1)` x7, `linear` x11, `ease-out` x2, `ease-in-out` x2, `steps(1)` x1, `cubic-bezier(0.2, 0.7, 0.3, 1)` x1. No --duration/--ease token is ever defined; no transition/animation reads a var().
confirmed.user_impact: Motion reads as inconsistent rather than one system - hover feedback at 0.12s next to 0.15s next to 0.16s, entrances at 0.22s/0.35s/0.5s/0.55s - and the same physical duration expressed in ms and s means a global retiming cannot be done in one place. The execution fails the 'one quiet system-wide motion' intent the code comments claim.
confirmed.fix: Introduce a small motion token scale in :root and route every transition/animation through it. Proposed: --dur-fast: 120ms (hover/color/border feedback), --dur-base: 200ms (small state changes), --dur-entrance: 400ms (element entrances), --dur-slow: 600ms (section reveal); --ease-standard: cubic-bezier(0.2,0.7,0.2,1) (already dominant at 7 uses), --ease-exit: ease-out, --ease-loop: linear (shimmer/blink). Collapse the 16 durations onto those four, pick one unit (ms), and replace bare `ease`.
confirmed.correction: A motion-token scale is not one of the owner's three explicitly-locked yardsticks (radius, breakpoints, colour-from-var), so this is adjacent/inferred rather than a mandated defect; the objective part (identical duration spelled two ways) is a genuine consistency defect but is closer to low than medium against the locked identity.

confirmed.title: Transition of a non-composited property (padding-left) will jank on animation
confirmed.evidence: `transition: padding-left 0.15s, color 0.15s;` (globals.css:7524). Also @keyframes shimmer animates `background-position` (globals.css:2929), which is likewise not GPU-composited.
confirmed.user_impact: Animating padding-left triggers layout on every frame (reflow of the element content), which can stutter on lower-end devices; the shimmer background-position repaints but is the accepted skeleton technique so is lower concern.
confirmed.fix: Replace the animated padding-left with a composited transform: transition transform: translateX(...) for the hover indent instead of padding-left, or move the indent to an inner element so only transform animates. Leave shimmer as-is unless the repaint proves costly.
confirmed.correction: Impact is negligible in practice: a single hovered link nudging 10px will not perceptibly jank on any modern device, and the auditor already concedes the shimmer background-position is the accepted skeleton technique. Real mechanism, but borderline as a reportable defect.

A spacing-token scale is the auditor's own extension and is not part of the approved identity, so this is a general maintainability observation rather than an identity-execution defect; severity lowered from high.

refuted.title: The hero and footer wordmark crops use different ratios (0.62em vs 0.60em), so the repeated signature does not match, and both sever the baseline of the round letters.
refuted.evidence:
.hero-wordmark span { ... height: 0.62em; }  /* line 6360 */
.footer-wordmark span { ... height: 0.6em; }  /* line 6227 */
refuted.user_impact: The crop is deliberate, but the two instances are not the same crop. The hero span is `clamp(90px,16.5vw,300px)` clipped to `height: 0.62em` (at a 900px viewport: 148.5px type, 92.1px visible band = 62%); the footer span is `clamp(80px,15vw,280px)` clipped to `height: 0.6em` (at 900px: 135px type, 81px band = 60%). Different type size AND different ratio means the two 'horizon-line' wordmarks read as two different treatments, not one signature echoed. Separately, both ratios cut below the x-height and through the baseline, severing the bottom curves of o/u/b/d/x and removing the baseline the word should rest on; the preserved ascenders (l/d/b/k) are fine, it is the bottoms that are cut.
refuted.fix: Unify both spans to a single crop ratio. To keep the signature identical, use the same `height` em value in both rules. To also stop severing the baseline of a light lowercase grotesk (baseline sits ~0.72-0.78em in a line-height:1 box), raise the crop to ~0.72em-0.78em rather than 0.60-0.62em; if the tighter horizon is intended, at minimum make hero and footer share one value.
refuted.correction: Facts (lines/values) are correct but the framing as a defect fails: the crop and the size difference are deliberate, and the 0.02em ratio gap is not perceptible. Not an execution failure of the identity.

refuted.title: The masthead nav clips via a deliberately hidden scrollbar, not a missing min-width; the fix is to stop hiding overflow and shed the duplicate action.
refuted.user_impact: Nav items are truncated ("erview", "settin") at every width with no scrollbar or fade to signal there is more, so links are simply unreachable and the header looks broken rather than scrollable.
refuted.fix: Mechanism confirmed: min-width:0 is ALREADY present (line 497), so the 1fr track shrinks correctly — the owner's 'missing min-width:0' hypothesis is REFUTED. The clip is the intentional overflow-x:auto (498) plus suppressed scrollbar (500, 507-509), which kernel.css never resets. Within the locked identity: (a) drop overflow-x:auto and let the nav collapse into the existing mobile-menu affordance at the 900px breakpoint instead of clipping silently, and (b) remove one of the two 'New Run' buttons from .masthead-actions to reclaim ~90px for the nav track. Also collapse the three conflicting .topbar-inner max-widths (globals 1440 @446, globals 1240 @2962, kernel 1200 @212) to one value so the available nav width is predictable.
refuted.correction: Duplicate of confirmed finding #1; not a fresh finding. Its one new sub-claim ('shed the duplicate action') is really finding #4's two 'New Run' buttons, not a nav-overflow matter.
